answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable stake before accessing shared work, then randomly assign tasks and check answers against verified results. Fake identities must each lock stake, so splitting one account does not create influence for free; provably false submissions lose deposits. This makes a sybil attack costly, though a wealthy attacker may still afford it. A plume of violet light at the zenith can mark the dashboard, but security comes from collateral and penalties.
